collection.description: A younger villager asks a man what makes someone a good man.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A younger villager asks (name1) what makes someone a good man. He has heard that men must never cry, must always be strong, and must someday become fathers. The man considers the people he admires and the mistakes he has made.

choices.label: Speak About Treating People with Respect
Speak About Responsibility to Loved Ones
Ask the Younger Villager What They Think

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: He explains that strength means little if it is used to belittle others.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: The younger villager asks whether respect includes people one disagrees with, and they discuss how to disagree without cruelty.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: He admits that he has cried, feared failure, and asked for help; the younger villager seems relieved.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: He struggles to find the words, realizing that he is still learning to express his emotions himself.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: He says that if someone chooses to build a family, showing up and sharing the work matter more than appearing powerful.

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: The younger villager asks about men without families, and he replies that no one must marry or have children to be a good man.

d1.name: Outcome D1
d1.text: Their answer surprises him, and he learns something from the conversation too.

d2.name: Outcome D2
d2.text: They disagree on several ideas, but both leave with more to consider.
